title: Async-to-sync cancellation needs an explicit outcome before notification
applies_when: A Python coroutine bridge stores a result or exception in a slot and signals an event in finally, while a blocking caller interprets an untouched slot as a successful None result.
lesson: Trace the outcome channel as well as the wakeup. Since Python 3.8, asyncio.CancelledError derives from BaseException, so except Exception does not publish it. A finally notification can wake the blocking caller while its result slot still contains the initial None. Reproduce through the complete imported bridge and a real generated synchronous backend method, not a copied catch block. Preserve normal values, original ordinary exceptions, cancellation cleanup and a subsequent healthy call. If the bridge already has an exception-delivery contract, explicitly store CancelledError so that existing caller-side propagation can raise it; do not equate a set event with successful completion. When downstream tests fail, check where cancellation is injected: patching a shared asyncio module can cancel metadata discovery before the claimed cleanup path. Scope the injection to the target module, cancel once, drain real writes, assert the returned cancellation outcome and partial-file cleanup, and use a suppression mutant as a negative control.
avoid_when: Do not catch all BaseException merely to cover asyncio cancellation: KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit can have different control-flow contracts. A backend cancelling itself and a synchronous caller interrupting a running backend are opposite directions; similar cancellation wording does not establish duplicate ownership. Transporting a cancellation outcome does not add cancellation requests, wait for every child task, force-stop blocking I/O or prove bulk-operation cleanup. The proposed bridge fix remains Draft after one real GCSFS downstream CI failure. Its original test was independently reproduced as failing in metadata lookup; proposed GCSFS1113 reaches actual cleanup and passes ten adjacent Linux/emulator cases with both old and fixed bridges. A separate EOF retry case timed out at 30 seconds on both versions and is explicitly excluded from that ten-case claim. Neither changing test scope nor focused emulator passes resolve maintainer acceptance, complete CI or real-cloud compatibility. Do not suppress propagation or weaken assertions for green checks. No general recall/cost or prospective selector advantage is established.

evidence.note: Documents cancellation semantics and the BaseException inheritance change in Python 3.8. Catching ordinary Exception alone therefore cannot populate a cancellation outcome.
Pinned _runner publishes only Exception then always signals its event; sync starts with a None slot and already propagates stored BaseException objects. This identifies the complete bridge mechanism.

One-line explicit cancellation handling plus direct/task/backend regressions. Six-case Linux original/fixed comparison and 190-pass Windows selection pass, but actual GCSFS CI has one injected-cancellation expectation failure (986 passes). Held as Draft pending downstream semantic compatibility; the native mechanism is not a certificate of accepted integration.

Distinct proposal cancels the submitted future when the synchronous event wait raises KeyboardInterrupt. It does not implement worker-to-caller cancellation outcome delivery; neither proposal establishes safety of every combined platform path.

Downstream test patches asyncio.wait to raise CancelledError, then calls synchronous get_file without accepting it. The failing integration trace reaches _info before the download-finally path mentioned by the test. Read the actual expectation and reachability before changing tests or declaring the behavior intentional.

Test-only correction with actual Linux fake-gcs-server HTTP/SDK execution: a ten-case selection including the two revised cancellation/control cases passes with old/fixed fsspec. Suppressing the production cancellation flag in a separate derived source fails the new outcome assertion while its normal control passes. Original test passes only on old bridge. No real GCS/full CI claim; larger selections preserve an EOF-retry timeout on both versions.

Pinned proposed test scopes asyncio replacement to core instead of globally replacing the shared module's wait; asserts pending to_thread writes, complete bytes before cleanup, cancellation outcome and final path ownership. A test-source proposal, not a production bugfix or merged contract.
